decisions.reason: Use full-sample breakpoints because the cited evidence states asset-growth decile cutoffs but does not state NYSE-only cutoffs for ASSETG.

paper_evidence.location: Table II caption p.1617; Section II.A p.1622
paper_evidence.quote: "formed based on June(t) asset growth decile cutoffs"; "using the 30th and 70th NYSE market equity percentiles"
paper_evidence.interpretation: The first quote supports decile cutoffs for ASSETG; the second quote limits explicit NYSE breakpoint language to size grouping. The exact ASSETG breakpoint universe is therefore unspecified in the paper text.

decisions.reason: Drop non-computable observations because the cited evidence requires nonzero assets in both required years.

paper_evidence.location: Section I Data p.1613; Appendix p.1648
paper_evidence.quote: "a firm must have nonzero total assets in both years t−1 and t−2"
paper_evidence.interpretation: The paper does not state general imputation; this requirement implies dropping observations without usable nonzero assets for ASSETG.

old_value.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spread comparisons but does not explicitly define a tradable simple long-short strategy. Direction is inferred for backtesting from the negative high-minus-low spread / high ASSETG -> low returns relation.

new_value.note: Paper reports high-minus-low spread comparisons but does not explicitly define a tradable simple long-short strategy. Direction is inferred for backtesting from the negative high-minus-low spread / high ASSETG -> low returns relation.

decisions.reason: Use the inferred long-low short-high direction because the cited evidence says low growth minus high growth is the return spread.

paper_evidence.location: Section II.A p.1622; Figure 3 caption p.1626
paper_evidence.quote: "The spread is the difference between the returns of the low growth stocks and those of the high growth stocks."
paper_evidence.interpretation: The paper compares low-growth and high-growth portfolios; long-low/short-high is an implementation inference for factor backtesting.

decisions.reason: Use no winsorization for the main portfolio spec because the cited evidence says winsorization appears only in regression robustness.

paper_evidence.quote: "we winsorize the asset growth distribution at the 1% and 99% points"
paper_evidence.interpretation: Winsorization is mentioned only for a regression robustness check, not the main portfolio-sort specification; therefore main-spec bounds are null.
